methodNote: Refute-not-confirm. The decisive test was not on the subject's internal consistency, which is high, nor on its bytes, which are sound and correctly described. It was on the standing of the member itself. The subject's three narrative authority fields each attribute their construction to one source, DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md axis E item 27. That is the only file the subject names without pinning a digest for it, so it was resolved directly: it is untracked, never committed, anchored to HEAD 8bc9963f and to g21-leftover-join.v13, and states of itself that it decides nothing. Following that thread to the recorded record rather than to the packet surfaced the recorded owner ruling at D-314 item 26, adopted after that HEAD, which orders this exact member skipped. The lineage's own doesNot strings were then diffed across all four recorded corpora against the subject's, which shows the disclaimer that carries that ruling being narrowed from the operative bound to the postHandshake bound alone.

findings.title: The subject first-authors the exactly-at member that a standing recorded owner decision orders left named-open and skipped, on a precondition the subject itself states is unmet, and it narrows the recorded disclaimer that carries that order from the operative bound to the postHandshake bound alone
findings.claimUnderReview: The subject authors G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake as the prefix integer of the CC-5 exactly-at limb against the preHandshake bound, and carries the disclaimer 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound.' at $.doesNot[36], with the matching failsIf and whatIsNotAuthored entries scoped the same way.
primaryEvidence: COORD, recorded heading D-314 (line 17981, 'User decisions: adopt the agreed G-owner-residuals recommendations', **ADOPTED 2026-08-29**, 'Made directly by the user in conversation. Same class as D-000 / D-054 / D-132 / D-293: the decisions are the user's, recorded verbatim rather than made on their behalf'), item 26, verbatim: '26. **G21-EXACT.** Leave the exactly-at member named-open and skip it until a control-protocol successor reconciles the class intent with the operative refusal predicate.'

The same recorded entry's next item shows the two halves were ruled on separately and deliberately: '27. **G21-POST.** Leave the postHandshake-bound members named-open and skip them until governing bytes pin both the negotiated fixture value and the fixture representation for postHandshake state.' Item 26 is therefore not a postHandshake item; it is the item that governs what the subject authors.

COORD, recorded heading D-315 (line 18147), confirms item 26 is still standing, verbatim: 'One id (G21-SCHEMA) supersedes D-314 item 28 only; D-314 items 1-27, 29 and 30 stand as recorded.' Item 26 is inside 1-27.

The precondition in item 26 is unmet, and the subject says so itself. $.registerRowNote: 'N=65536 is not pinned as prefix-only RF-2 because the quoted preHandshake clause and CC-5 intent disagree about N=65536.' $.authorityClaim: 'CC-5 intent types prefix exactly at as RF-2. N=65536 is not pinned as prefix-only RF-2. That tension is not settled by authoring the prefix integer.' That unreconciled disagreement between the class intent and the operative refusal predicate is word-for-word the condition item 26 requires a control-protocol successor to resolve first.

No control-protocol successor exists. docs/coop/artifacts/ holds control-protocol-contract.v1.json and control-protocol-contract.v2.json and no later version, and the subject itself cites v2 (c50a79fe…, D-015) as the consumed contract at $.basedOn.controlProtocolV2.

Every recorded G21 decision heading since that ruling recites the prohibition verbatim as a live constraint on its own act: D-351 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.'; D-352 (the recorded truncated-body corpus) 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.'; D-353 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.' and 'Prefix exactly at the operative bound remains a named open decision.'; D-358 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.'

The live governing join the subject is based on keeps the member unauthored. leftover-join.v45 of G21 (D-359) $.obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.remainingCc5Injections[0] is 'CC-5 prefix exactly at the operative bound', and the D-359 COORD entry reads 'leftover-design of remaining CC-5 injections remains, including prefix exactly at the operative bound.'

The lineage's own doesNot strings show the narrowing. Every recorded corpus carries the wide form verbatim: g21-fixture-corpus.v26 (D-352), v30 (D-354), v31 (D-356) and v33 (D-358) each carry 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.' The subject replaces it with 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound.' — the same narrowing the frozen, REJECTed g21-fixture-corpus.v34 carried. $.failsIf[16] and $.whatIsNotAuthored[7] are narrowed to match, so the document's own failure conditions can no longer detect the act.

The subject cites neither D-314 nor D-315 nor the G21-EXACT ruling anywhere; grep for 'D-314', 'D-315' and 'G21-EXACT' across the document returns nothing. Its basedOn set stops at D-293 for owner decisions and otherwise carries only D-352 through D-359.
findings.impact: This is the authoring act itself, not a wording defect around it. A standing owner ruling, made directly by the user and confirmed still standing by a later owner ruling, says this member is named-open and is to be skipped until a control-protocol successor reconciles the class intent with the operative refusal predicate. No such successor exists, the subject states in three places that the reconciliation has not happened, and it authors the member anyway. The narrowed disclaimer at $.doesNot[36] is what carries the breach through the document: because the wide form every recorded corpus carries has been replaced by a postHandshake-only form, the subject reads internally as compliant while doing the one thing the ruling forbids, and its own failsIf list cannot catch it. Recording this would put a first-authoring of an owner-blocked member into the record under a register row whose live token is OPEN, and would leave the next leftover-join remasurement measuring leftover-design of a member the owner had ordered skipped. It also explains, and is not answered by, the history: the byte-identical member was dual-REJECTed at g21-fixture-corpus.v9 and REJECTed again at g21-fixture-corpus.v34, each time on a downstream symptom of the same unreconciled predicate that item 26 names as the reason to wait.
findings.notWhatIsBeingAsked: This finding does NOT dispute the payload bytes, which are sound, correctly decoded, correctly distinguished from every earlier-authored prefix, and byte-identical to the two frozen copies as the dispatch states. It does not dispute the CC-5 limb, the member id, the input-corpus id or the path. It does not ask that N=65536 be pinned as prefix-only RF-2, and it does not ask that the observable refusal route be pinned — the subject is right to decline both. It does not re-raise CLAUDE-G21FXV34-M-1 or CLAUDE-G21FXV34-S-1, which landed as specified. The defect is that the member is authored at all while the recorded condition for authoring it is unmet, and that the disclaimer which would have disclosed that has been narrowed.
findings.requiredRemedy: A successor must not first-author the exactly-at member while D-314 item 26 stands and no control-protocol successor has reconciled the class intent with the operative refusal predicate. It should restore the wide disclaimer 'Does not first-author prefix exactly at the operative bound.' to doesNot, with failsIf and whatIsNotAuthored scoped to the operative bound rather than to the postHandshake bound alone, matching recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v26, v30, v31 and v33. If the intent is to keep these bytes on disk, the successor may catalog them as an unauthored named-open witness that the ruling reserves, naming D-314 item 26 and D-315's 'items 1-27, 29 and 30 stand as recorded' in basedOn and pinning both, and stating that leftover-design of the member remains open and is not made stale by the bytes existing. Preserve the frozen payload and the frozen fixtures/g21.v9/ and fixtures/g21.v26/ copies during repair. If the author believes item 26 has been lifted, that lift is a recorded decision this reviewer could not find, and it must be cited by heading and pinned rather than assumed.

findings.title: The sole authority the subject offers for its construction is the one file it names without pinning: an untracked, never-committed working document anchored to a superseded HEAD that states of itself that it decides nothing
findings.claimUnderReview: Three narrative authority fields each end the construction argument with the same clause: 'sanctioned at DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md axis E item 27'. $.proposedLaterWork[4] further conditions a later authoring step on that packet's open question: 'A later leftover-design cycle may author delivery of 65536 body bytes if OQ-G21-4 is settled.'
primaryEvidence: DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md disclaims exactly the authority the word 'sanctioned' attributes to it. Its own second paragraph, verbatim: 'Recorded at HEAD `8bc9963f68784842de643d5dbb1269bd4cf4411a`. This is an inventory of already-recorded bytes. It authors no fixture byte, records no successor, and decides nothing.'

It has no recorded standing. `git ls-files --error-unmatch DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md` fails — the file is untracked and appears in no commit — and grep for 'D1-plan' across docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md returns nothing.

It is anchored behind the live record. Its stated HEAD 8bc9963f is 'D-293 hygiene: mark DECISIONS-NEEDED decided and STATUS pushed', dated 2026-08-28, 66 commits behind live HEAD 5a45ebf2, and its governing-bytes section pins g21-leftover-join.v13 (D-292) where the live governing join is leftover-join.v45 of G21 (D-359). The recorded owner ruling at issue in CLAUDE-G21FXV35-M-1, D-314, was adopted 2026-08-29 — after that HEAD — so the packet cannot and does not account for it.

It is the only cited file the subject does not pin. Of every path named in the document that exists on disk, all are pinned by digest in recordedInputs or by a path/sha256 pair except DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md and the doesNotMutate directory strings, which are directories and carry no digest by established practice. 49 of 49 recordedInputs entries and 37 of 37 structured pairs recompute clean; this one file has no digest anywhere in the document.

Because it is unpinned it is also outside the document's own guard. $.remeasurementClause enumerates the cited files that must be remeasured before recording — file 08, leftover-join.v45 of G21, leftover-join.v14 of sarif, g21-fixture-corpus.v33/v31/v30/v26, occupancy v4, control-protocol-contract.v2, the payload bytes, frozen g21-fixture-corpus.v34 and v9 — and does not include this packet, so a mutation of the one unpinned authority would pass the subject's own remeasurement test.

No candidate in this lineage has cited it before. grep for 'D1-plan' across g21-fixture-corpus.v26, v30, v31, v33 and v34 returns zero hits in all five; the subject is the first candidate of record to introduce the citation, and it introduces it three times in the three fields that carry its authority argument.

OQ-G21-4 itself is not the problem and is not being challenged: the token is recorded in COORD, which the subject pins, at D-314 item 28 ('pending the OQ-G21-4 fixture-form ruling') and again in the D-315 G21-SCHEMA text. The defect is confined to the unpinned packet and to the word 'sanctioned'.
findings.impact: The document is otherwise scrupulous about provenance — it pins peripheral files as minor as the g21-fixture-corpus.v10 Codex review — so a reader is entitled to read 'sanctioned at' as naming an authority of the same grade. It is not one: it is an uncommitted working inventory, built before the owner ruling that governs this member, which says in its own text that it decides nothing. A later D-000 recording would be recording an authority claim that cannot be verified from the record, on the one file whose bytes nothing fixes. This finding stands on its own as a provenance defect, and it is also the route by which CLAUDE-G21FXV35-M-1 was reached: the construction was justified against a stale packet instead of against the live recorded decisions, and the live recorded decisions forbid it.
findings.notWhatIsBeingAsked: This finding does not assert that the citation is factually inaccurate. DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md axis E item 27 does read as the subject reports it, and its line 1086 does say that every remaining CC-5 injection except 'prefix exactly at' and 'prefix far over' requires a body. Nor does it ask that OQ-G21-4 be dropped; that token is recorded in pinned COORD bytes and is used correctly.
findings.requiredRemedy: A successor should either drop the three 'sanctioned at' clauses and rest the construction on sources it already pins — the quoted control-protocol-contract.v2 preHandshake bound and frame rule, and the on-disk analogue bytes at fixtures/g21.v3/ and fixtures/g21.v4/ whose digests it already carries — or, if it keeps the citation, pin DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md by digest in recordedInputs, add it to the remeasurementClause, and describe it as what it says it is: an unrecorded inventory anchored at HEAD 8bc9963f and at g21-leftover-join.v13, which authors nothing and decides nothing, rather than as a sanction. Whichever route is taken, the live recorded decisions that do govern the member must be cited and pinned; see CLAUDE-G21FXV35-M-1.
